sanskrit: sa dadarśāsane rāmo niṣaṇṇaṃ pitaraṃ śubhe kaikeyīsahitaṃ dīnaṃ mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: Rāma saw his father seated on the auspicious throne, desolate, accompanied by Kaikeyī, his face withered and parched.

sanskrit: sa pituś caraṇau pūrvam abhivādya vinītavat tato vavande caraṇau kaikeyyāḥ susamāhitaḥ
english: He first reverently saluted his father's feet in the customary humble manner, then composed, he also paid obeisance to the feet of Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: rāmety uktvā ca vacanaṃ vāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ śaśāka nṛpatir dīno nekṣituṃ nābhibhāṣitum
english: Having uttered only the word "Rāma," with eyes overwhelmed by tears, the wretched king was unable either to look at him or to speak to him.

sanskrit: tad apūrvaṃ narapater dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ bhayāvaham rāmo 'pi bhayam āpannaḥ padā spṛṣṭveva pannagam
english: Seeing that unprecedented, terrifying aspect of the lord of men, Rāma too was seized with fear, as though he had touched a serpent with his foot.

sanskrit: indriyair aprahṛṣṭais taṃ śokasaṃtāpakarśitam niḥśvasantaṃ mahārājaṃ vyathitākulacetasaṃ
english: With senses joyless, he beheld the great king, emaciated by grief and anguish, sighing heavily, his mind troubled and distraught.

sanskrit: ūrmi mālinam akṣobhyaṃ kṣubhyantam iva sāgaram upaplutam ivādityam uktānṛtam ṛṣiṃ yathā
english: He was like the ocean, ordinarily unshakeable yet now agitated with waves; like the sun eclipsed; like a sage made to utter an untruth.

sanskrit: acintyakalpaṃ hi pitus taṃ śokam upadhārayan babhūva saṃrabdhataraḥ samudra iva parvaṇi
english: Perceiving the inconceivable, extraordinary grief of his father, Rāma became more agitated, like the ocean at the full moon.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa ca tadā rāmaḥ pitṛhite rataḥ kiṃsvid adyaiva nṛpatir na māṃ pratyabhinandati
english: Then Rāma, ever devoted to his father's welfare, began to reflect: "Why does the king today not welcome me as he usually does?"

sanskrit: anyadā māṃ pitā dṛṣṭvā kupito 'pi prasīdati tasya mām adya saṃprekṣya kimāyāsaḥ pravartate
english: "At other times, even when angry, my father grows pleased upon seeing me — what distress has come upon him today when he looks at me?"

sanskrit: sa dīna iva śokārto viṣaṇṇavadanadyutiḥ kaikeyīm abhivādyaiva rāmo vacanam abravīt
english: Rāma, looking as though wretched, stricken with sorrow, the radiance of his face dimmed, saluted Kaikeyī and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: kaccin mayā nāparāddham ajñānād yena me pitā kupitas tan mamācakṣva tvaṃ caivainaṃ prasādaya
english: "Have I unknowingly committed some offense because of which my father is angry? Tell me that, and do you yourself appease him."

sanskrit: vivarṇavadano dīno na hi mām abhibhāṣate śārīro mānaso vāpi kaccid enaṃ na bādhate saṃtāpo vābhitāpo vā durlabhaṃ hi sadā sukham
english: "Wretched, with face drained of colour, he does not speak to me — is there no bodily or mental affliction, no grief or burning anguish troubling him? For happiness is always hard to attain."

sanskrit: kaccin na kiṃ cid bharate kumāre priyadarśane śatrughne vā mahāsattve mātṝṇāṃ vā mamāśubham
english: "Has nothing inauspicious befallen prince Bharata of lovely form, or mighty Śatrughna, or any of my mothers?"

sanskrit: atoṣayan mahārājam akurvan vā pitur vacaḥ muhūrtam api neccheyaṃ jīvituṃ kupite nṛpe
english: "If I have failed to please the great king or have not acted on my father's words, I would not wish to live even for a moment while the king is angry."

sanskrit: yatomūlaṃ naraḥ paśyet prādurbhāvam ihātmanaḥ kathaṃ tasmin na varteta pratyakṣe sati daivate
english: "How should one not honor him through whom a person sees the origin of his own existence here in this world — he being a visible divinity before one's eyes?"

sanskrit: kaccit te paruṣaṃ kiṃ cid abhimānāt pitā mama ukto bhavatyā kopena yatrāsya lulitaṃ manaḥ
english: "Has my father perhaps been addressed by you with harsh words born of pride, spoken in anger, words that have agitated his mind?"

sanskrit: etad ācakṣva me devi tattvena paripṛcchataḥ kiṃnimittam apūrvo 'yaṃ vikāro manujādhipe
english: "Tell me truthfully, O queen, as I earnestly ask — what is the cause of this unprecedented change in the lord of men?"

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi vacanād rājñaḥ pateyam api pāvake bhakṣayeyaṃ viṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ majjeyam api cārṇave niyukto guruṇā pitrā nṛpeṇa ca hitena ca
english: "At the king's command I would leap into fire, drink sharp poison, or plunge into the sea — when directed to do so by my revered father, the king who wishes my good."

sanskrit: tad brūhi vacanaṃ devi rājño yad abhikāṅkṣitam kariṣye pratijāne ca rāmo dvir nābhibhāṣate
english: "Therefore speak, O queen, whatever the king desires — I shall do it, and I swear to it: Rāma does not speak twice."

sanskrit: tam ārjavasamāyuktam anāryā satyavādinam uvāca rāmaṃ kaikeyī vacanaṃ bhṛśadāruṇam
english: To Rāma, who was thus full of sincerity and truthful in speech, the ignoble Kaikeyī spoke words that were exceedingly cruel.

sanskrit: purā devāsure yuddhe pitrā te mama rāghava rakṣitena varau dattau saśalyena mahāraṇe
english: "Long ago, O Rāghava, in the war between gods and demons, your father, having protected me when I was wounded in that great battle, granted me two boons.

sanskrit: tatra me yācito rājā bharatasyābhiṣecanam gamanaṃ daṇḍakāraṇye tava cādyaiva rāghava
english: "From those boons I have asked the king: the consecration of Bharata as crown prince, and your departure, this very day, O Rāghava, to the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: yadi satyapratijñaṃ tvaṃ pitaraṃ kartum icchasi ātmānaṃ ca narareṣṭha mama vākyam idaṃ śṛṇu
english: "If you wish to keep your father true to his pledge, and to maintain your own honor, O foremost of men, then hear these words of mine."

sanskrit: sa nideśe pitus tiṣṭha yathā tena pratiśrutam tvayāraṇyaṃ praveṣṭavyaṃ nava varṣāṇi pañca ca
english: "Abide by your father's command as he has promised on your behalf: you are to enter the forest for nine years and five years — fourteen years in all."

sanskrit: sapta sapta ca varṣāṇi daṇḍakāraṇyam āśritaḥ abhiṣekam imaṃ tyaktvā jaṭācīradharo vasa
english: "Seven and seven years dwelling in the Daṇḍaka wilderness, abandoning this consecration, you shall live clad in matted locks and bark garments."

sanskrit: bharataḥ kosalapure praśāstu vasudhām imām nānāratnasamākīrṇāṃ savājirathakuñjarām
english: "Let Bharata rule this earth, rich in diverse gems and furnished with horses, chariots, and elephants, from the city of Kosala."

sanskrit: tad apriyam amitraghno vacanaṃ maraṇopamam śrutvā na vivyathe rāmaḥ kaikeyīṃ cedam abravīt
english: Hearing those unpleasant words, words equivalent to death, Rāma, slayer of enemies, was not disturbed, and he said this to Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: evam astu gamiṣyāmi vanaṃ vastum ahaṃ tv ataḥ jaṭācīradharo rājñaḥ pratijñām anupālayan
english: "So be it. I shall go from here to dwell in the forest, wearing matted locks and bark garments, upholding the king's pledge."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu jñātum icchāmi kimarthaṃ māṃ mahīpatiḥ nābhinandati durdharṣo yathāpuram ariṃdamaḥ
english: "But this I wish to know: why does the lord of the earth, the invincible subduer of enemies, not welcome me as before?"

sanskrit: manyur na ca tvayā kāryo devi brūhi tavāgrataḥ yāsyāmi bhava suprītā vanaṃ cīrajaṭādharaḥ
english: "Do not feel anger, O queen. Speak before you. I shall go — be well pleased — to the forest wearing bark garments and matted locks."

sanskrit: hitena guruṇā pitrā kṛtajñena nṛpeṇa ca niyujyamāno viśrabdhaṃ kiṃ na kuryād ahaṃ priyam
english: "What pleasing act would I not confidently perform when directed by my beneficent elder, my grateful father the king?"

sanskrit: alīkaṃ mānasaṃ tv ekaṃ hṛdayaṃ dahatīva me svayaṃ yan nāha māṃ rājā bharatasyābhiṣecanam
english: "Yet one false thing in my heart burns me as with fire: that the king did not himself tell me of Bharata's consecration."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi sītāṃ rājyaṃ ca prāṇān iṣṭān dhanāni ca hṛṣṭo bhrātre svayaṃ dadyāṃ bharatāyāpracoditaḥ
english: "For I would gladly give of my own accord — without being prompted — Sītā, the kingdom, my cherished life, and my wealth to my brother Bharata."

sanskrit: kiṃ punar manujendreṇa svayaṃ pitrā pracoditaḥ tava ca priyakāmārthaṃ pratijñām anupālayan
english: "How much more so when directed by the lord of men, my own father, and when upholding a pledge for the sake of fulfilling your desire?"

sanskrit: tad āśvāsaya hīmaṃ tvaṃ kiṃ nv idaṃ yan mahīpatiḥ vasudhāsaktanayano mandam aśrūṇi muñcati
english: "So console him — why does the lord of the earth keep his gaze fixed on the ground and weep these slow tears?"

sanskrit: gacchantu caivānayituṃ dūtāḥ śīghrajavair hayaiḥ bharataṃ mātulakulād adyaiva nṛpaśāsanāt
english: "Let messengers go this very day, by the king's command, on swift horses, to bring Bharata from his maternal uncle's home."

sanskrit: daṇḍakāraṇyam eṣo 'ham ito gacchāmi satvaraḥ avicārya pitur vākyaṃ samāvastuṃ caturdaśa
english: "As for me, I depart swiftly from here to the Daṇḍaka forest, without deliberating over my father's words, to dwell there for fourteen years."

sanskrit: sā hṛṣṭā tasya tadvākyaṃ śrutvā rāmasya kaikayī prasthānaṃ śraddadhānā hi tvarayām āsa rāghavam
english: Kaikeyī, delighted upon hearing those words of Rāma, believing his departure certain, urged Rāghava to set out without delay.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhavatu yāsyanti dūtāḥ śīghrajavair hayaiḥ bharataṃ mātulakulād upāvartayituṃ narāḥ
english: "So be it: men shall go on swift horses to bring Bharata back from his maternal uncle's family."

sanskrit: tava tv ahaṃ kṣamaṃ manye notsukasya vilambanam rāma tasmād itaḥ śīghraṃ vanaṃ tvaṃ gantum arhasi
english: "But for you, who are not eager to linger, I think delay is not proper, Rāma — therefore you ought to depart swiftly to the forest from here."

sanskrit: vrīḍānvitaḥ svayaṃ yac ca nṛpas tvāṃ nābhibhāṣate naitat kiṃ cin naraśreṣṭha manyur eṣo 'panīyatām
english: "And that the king, filled with shame, does not speak to you himself — this is nothing at all, O foremost of men; let this anger be set aside."

sanskrit: yāvat tvaṃ na vanaṃ yātaḥ purād asmād abhitvaran pitā tāvan na te rāma snāsyate bhokṣyate 'pi vā
english: "As long as you have not departed swiftly to the forest from this city, Rāma, your father will neither bathe nor eat."

sanskrit: dhik kaṣṭam iti niḥśvasya rājā śokapariplutaḥ mūrchito nyapatat tasmin paryaṅke hemabhūṣite
english: Sighing, "Alas, what misery!" the king, overwhelmed with grief, fell unconscious on that gold-adorned couch.

sanskrit: rāmo 'py utthāpya rājānaṃ kaikeyyābhipracoditaḥ kaśayevāhato vājī vanaṃ gantuṃ kṛtatvaraḥ
english: Rāma, urged on by Kaikeyī, raised the king up, and like a horse struck by a whip, made haste to depart to the forest.

sanskrit: tad apriyam anāryāyā vacanaṃ dāruṇodaram śrutvā gatavyatho rāmaḥ kaikeyīṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Having heard that cruel, deeply unpleasant speech of the ignoble woman, Rāma, free from distress, spoke these words to Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: nāham arthaparo devi lokam āvastum utsahe viddhi mām ṛṣibhis tulyaṃ kevalaṃ dharmam āsthitam
english: "I am not devoted to material gain, O queen, nor do I aspire to inhabit the world for that — know me as equal to the sages, standing solely by dharma."

sanskrit: yad atrabhavataḥ kiṃ cic chakyaṃ kartuṃ priyaṃ mayā prāṇān api parityajya sarvathā kṛtam eva tat
english: "Whatever agreeable thing it is possible for me to do for his honored self, even at the cost of giving up my life, that is in every way already done."

sanskrit: na hy ato dharmacaraṇaṃ kiṃ cid asti mahattaram yathā pitari śuśrūṣā tasya vā vacanakriyā
english: "For there is no practice of dharma greater than service to one's father and the fulfillment of his command."

sanskrit: anukto 'py atrabhavatā bhavatyā vacanād aham vane vatsyāmi vijane varṣāṇīha caturdaśa
english: "Even uninstructed by his honored self, at your word I shall dwell in the lonely forest here for fourteen years."

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ mayi kaikeyi kiṃ cid āśaṃsase guṇam yad rājānam avocas tvaṃ mameśvaratarā satī
english: "You truly expect no virtue in me at all, O Kaikeyī, that you — being more powerful than I — spoke to the king in this way on my behalf."

sanskrit: yāvan mātaram āpṛcche sītāṃ cānunayāmy aham tato 'dyaiva gamiṣyāmi daṇḍakānāṃ mahad vanam
english: "As soon as I take leave of my mother and comfort Sītā, I shall depart this very day to the great Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: bharataḥ pālayed rājyaṃ śuśrūṣec ca pitur yathā tathā bhavatyā kartavyaṃ sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: "Let Bharata rule the kingdom and serve his father as befits him — this too must be arranged by you, for that is eternal dharma."

sanskrit: sa rāmasya vacaḥ śrutvā bhṛśaṃ duḥkhahataḥ pitā śokād aśaknuvan bāṣpaṃ praruroda mahāsvanam
english: On hearing Rāma's words, the father, deeply stricken with pain, unable to hold back his tears from grief, wept aloud with a great cry.

sanskrit: vanditvā caraṇau rāmo visaṃjñasya pitus tadā kaikeyyāś cāpy anāryāyā niṣpapāta mahādyutiḥ
english: Having saluted the feet of his father who had lost consciousness, and the feet also of the ignoble Kaikeyī, the great-resplendent Rāma departed.

sanskrit: sa rāmaḥ pitaraṃ kṛtvā kaikeyīṃ ca pradakṣiṇam niṣkramyāntaḥpurāt tasmāt svaṃ dadarśa suhṛjjanam
english: Rāma, having circumambulated his father and Kaikeyī, stepped out of the inner apartments and saw his own circle of dear friends.

sanskrit: taṃ bāṣpaparipūrṇākṣaḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nujagāma ha lakṣmaṇaḥ paramakruddhaḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ
english: Eyes brimming with tears, utterly furious, Lakṣmaṇa, the increaser of Sumitrā's joy, followed behind him.

sanskrit: ābhiṣecanikaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ kṛtvā rāmaḥ pradakṣiṇam śanair jagāma sāpekṣo dṛṣṭiṃ tatrāvicālayan
english: Rāma circumambulated the consecration materials and walked slowly away, his gaze lingering, turning back with a longing look.

sanskrit: na cāsya mahatīṃ lakṣmīṃ rājyanāśo 'pakarṣati lokakāntasya kāntatvaṃ śītaraśmer iva kṣapā
english: The loss of the kingdom did not diminish his great splendor, just as the night does not diminish the loveliness of the cool-rayed moon that is beloved of the world.

sanskrit: na vanaṃ gantukāmasya tyajataś ca vasuṃdharām sarvalokātigasyeva lakṣyate cittavikriyā
english: In one wishing to go to the forest and relinquishing the earth, no perturbation of mind was apparent — as in one who has transcended all the worlds.

sanskrit: dhārayan manasā duḥkham indriyāṇi nigṛhya ca praviveśātmavān veśma māturapriyaśaṃsivān
english: Bearing the sorrow inwardly, restraining his senses, that self-possessed one entered his mother's dwelling, bearing the bearer of unwelcome tidings for her.

sanskrit: praviśya veśmātibhṛśaṃ mudānvitaṃ samīkṣya tāṃ cārthavipattim āgatām na caiva rāmo 'tra jagāma vikriyāṃ suhṛjjanasyātmavipattiśaṅkayā
english: Having entered and seeing the dwelling filled with great joy, and having become aware of the calamity that had come to pass, even there Rāma showed no perturbation, out of concern lest his dear ones be alarmed at his own misfortune.

sanskrit: rāmas tu bhṛśam āyasto niḥśvasann iva kuñjaraḥ jagāma sahito bhrātrā mātur antaḥpuraṃ vaśī
english: Rāma, greatly fatigued, sighing like an elephant, the self-restrained one went with his brother to his mother's inner apartments.

sanskrit: so 'paśyat puruṣaṃ tatra vṛddhaṃ paramapūjitam upaviṣṭaṃ gṛhadvāri tiṣṭhataś cāparān bahūn
english: There he saw an elderly man of great honor seated at the doorway of the house, and many others standing there as well.

sanskrit: praviśya prathamāṃ kakṣyāṃ dvitīyāyāṃ dadarśa saḥ brāhmaṇān vedasaṃpannān vṛddhān rājñābhisatkṛtān
english: Entering the first courtyard, in the second he saw aged Brāhmaṇas learned in the Vedas, honored by the king.

sanskrit: praṇamya rāmas tān vṛddhāṃs tṛtīyāyāṃ dadarśa saḥ striyo vṛddhāś ca bālāś ca dvārarakṣaṇatatparāḥ
english: Rāma bowed to those elders, and in the third courtyard he saw women — both old and young — intent on guarding the door.

sanskrit: vardhayitvā prahṛṣṭās tāḥ praviśya ca gṛhaṃ striyaḥ nyavedayanta tvaritā rāma mātuḥ priyaṃ tadā
english: Those delighted women greeted him and then swiftly entered the house and announced to Rāma's mother the joy of his arrival.

sanskrit: kausalyāpi tadā devī rātriṃ sthitvā samāhitā prabhāte tv akarot pūjāṃ viṣṇoḥ putrahitaiṣiṇī
english: Queen Kausalyā too, having kept vigil through the night in concentrated prayer, at dawn performed worship of Viṣṇu, she who desired her son's welfare.

sanskrit: sā kṣaumavasanā hṛṣṭā nityaṃ vrataparāyaṇā agniṃ juhoti sma tadā mantravat kṛtamaṅgalā
english: She, clad in a silk garment, joyful, ever devoted to vows, performed oblations into the sacred fire with mantras, having made all auspicious rites.

sanskrit: praviśya ca tadā rāmo mātur antaḥpuraṃ śubham dadarśa mātaraṃ tatra hāvayantīṃ hutāśanam
english: Then Rāma, entering his mother's auspicious inner apartments, saw his mother there engaged in making offerings to the sacred fire.

sanskrit: sā cirasyātmajaṃ dṛṣṭvā mātṛnandanam āgatam abhicakrāma saṃhṛṣṭā kiśoraṃ vaḍavā yathā
english: She, seeing her son who had long been awaited, the delight of his mother, now arrived, rushed forward overjoyed, as a mare rushes toward her young colt.

sanskrit: tam uvāca durādharṣaṃ rāghavaṃ sutam ātmanaḥ kausalyā putravātsalyād idaṃ priyahitaṃ vacaḥ
english: Kausalyā, out of maternal love for her son, spoke to that Rāghava, her invincible child, these words that were both affectionate and beneficial.

sanskrit: vṛddhānāṃ dharmaśīlānāṃ rājarṣīṇāṃ mahātmanām prāpnuhy āyuś ca kīrtiṃ ca dharmaṃ copahitaṃ kule
english: "May you attain the long life, glory, and dharma proper to the lineage of the noble, dharma-disciplined, great-souled royal sages."

sanskrit: satyapratijñaṃ pitaraṃ rājānaṃ paśya rāghava adyaiva hi tvāṃ dharmātmā yauvarājye 'bhiṣekṣyati
english: "Behold, O Rāghava, your father the king, true to his pledges — this very day the righteous-souled one shall consecrate you as crown prince."

sanskrit: mātaraṃ rāghavaḥ kiṃ cit prasāryāñjalim abravīt sa svabhāvavinītaś ca gauravāc ca tadānataḥ
english: Rāghava, extending his joined palms toward his mother, spoke to her — he who was naturally humble and now bent down in reverence.

sanskrit: devi nūnaṃ na jānīṣe mahad bhayam upasthitam idaṃ tava ca duḥkhāya vaidehyā lakṣmaṇasya ca
english: "O queen, you surely do not know that a great peril is at hand — one that will bring sorrow to you, to Vaidehī, and to Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi vatsyāmi vijane vane madhumūlaphalair jīvan hitvā munivad āmiṣam
english: "For fourteen years I shall dwell in the lonely forest, living on honey, roots, and fruits, having forsaken meat in the manner of a sage."

sanskrit: bharatāya mahārājo yauvarājyaṃ prayacchati māṃ punar daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ vivāsayati tāpasaṃ
english: "The great king grants the crown-princeship to Bharata, and banishes me — as an ascetic — to the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: tām aduḥkhocitāṃ dṛṣṭvā patitāṃ kadalīm iva rāmas tūtthāpayām āsa mātaraṃ gatacetasaṃ
english: Seeing her — unaccustomed to sorrow — fallen like a plantain tree, insensible, Rāma raised his mother up.

sanskrit: upāvṛtyotthitāṃ dīnāṃ vaḍavām iva vāhitām pāṃśuguṇṭhitasarvāgnīṃ vimamarśa ca pāṇinā
english: Having turned and raised her up — wretched as an overburdened mare — her every limb covered with dust, he stroked her with his hand.

sanskrit: sā rāghavam upāsīnam asukhārtā sukhocitā uvāca puruṣavyāghram upaśṛṇvati lakṣmaṇe
english: She, afflicted with sorrow, she who was accustomed to happiness, spoke to Rāghava who sat beside her — that tiger among men — while Lakṣmaṇa listened.

sanskrit: yadi putra na jāyethā mama śokāya rāghava na sma duḥkham ato bhūyaḥ paśyeyam aham aprajā
english: "O Rāghava, my son, if you had not been born for my grief, then I, being childless, would have seen no greater sorrow than that."

sanskrit: eka eva hi vandhyāyāḥ śoko bhavati mānavaḥ aprajāsmīti saṃtāpo na hy anyaḥ putra vidyate
english: "For a barren woman has only one human sorrow — the grief of 'I am without a child' — truly there is no other sorrow, my son."

sanskrit: na dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ kalyāṇaṃ sukhaṃ vā patipauruṣe api putre vipaśyeyam iti rāmāsthitaṃ mayā
english: "It was with the hope that I might behold good fortune or happiness through a husband's valor or through a son that I persevered, placing my faith in Rāma."

sanskrit: sā bahūny amanojñāni vākyāni hṛdayacchidām ahaṃ śroṣye sapatnīnām avarāṇāṃ varā satī ato duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ nu pramadānāṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "I, though the chief among co-wives, shall be forced to hear many unpleasant, heart-piercing words from those junior co-wives — what greater sorrow can there be for any woman?"

sanskrit: tvayi saṃnihite 'py evam aham āsaṃ nirākṛtā kiṃ punaḥ proṣite tāta dhruvaṃ maraṇam eva me
english: "Even with you present near me, I was thus rejected and ignored — what then when you are gone, my dear? Death alone is certain for me."

sanskrit: yo hi māṃ sevate kaś cid atha vāpy anuvartate kaikeyyāḥ putram anvīkṣya sa jano nābhibhāṣate
english: "Whoever serves me or follows my wishes, upon looking toward Kaikeyī's son, that person does not address me."

sanskrit: daśa sapta ca varṣāṇi tava jātasya rāghava atītāni prakāṅkṣantyā mayā duḥkhaparikṣayam
english: "Seventeen years since your birth have passed, O Rāghava, while I waited in expectation for the end of my sorrows."

sanskrit: upavāsaiś ca yogaiś ca bahubhiś ca pariśramaiḥ duḥkhaṃ saṃvardhito moghaṃ tvaṃ hi durgatayā mayā
english: "Through fastings, austerities, and many hardships — reared with difficulty you have been raised in vain by me in my misfortune."

sanskrit: sthiraṃ tu hṛdayaṃ manye mamedaṃ yan na dīryate prāvṛṣīva mahānadyāḥ spṛṣṭaṃ kūlaṃ navāmbhasā
english: "Firm indeed I deem my heart, that it does not break apart, like the bank of a great river touched by the new flood-waters of the rains."

sanskrit: mamaiva nūnaṃ maraṇaṃ na vidyate na cāvakāśo 'sti yamakṣaye mama yad antako 'dyaiva na māṃ jihīrṣati prasahya siṃho rudatīṃ mṛgīm iva
english: "Surely death does not exist for me, nor is there room for me in Yama's realm, since Death does not this very day carry me off by force, as a lion carries off a weeping doe."

sanskrit: sthiraṃ hi nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ mamāyasaṃ na bhidyate yad bhuvi nāvadīryate anena duḥkhena ca deham arpitaṃ dhruvaṃ hy akāle maraṇaṃ na vidyate
english: "My heart is surely firm as iron, that it does not shatter, that upon this earth it does not split asunder with this body given over to such grief — for truly, untimely death does not exist."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu duḥkhaṃ yad anarthakāni me vratāni dānāni ca saṃyamāś ca hi tapaś ca taptaṃ yad apatyakāraṇāt suniṣphalaṃ bījam ivoptam ūṣare
english: "This is my sorrow: that my vows, gifts, self-restraints, and austerities practiced for the sake of offspring are utterly fruitless — like good seed sown in barren soil."

sanskrit: yadi hy akāle maraṇaṃ svayecchayā labheta kaś cid guru duḥkha karśitaḥ gatāham adyaiva pareta saṃsadaṃ vinā tvayā dhenur ivātmajena vai
english: "If one could attain untimely death by one's own will when worn away by great sorrow, I would have gone this very day to the assembly of the dead, like a cow bereft of her own calf."

sanskrit: bhṛśam asukham amarṣitā tadā bahu vilalāpa samīkṣya rāghavam vyasanam upaniśāmya sā mahat sutam iva baddham avekṣya kiṃnarī
english: Deeply unhappy, overcome with indignation, she lamented much, gazing upon Rāghava, perceiving that great calamity — like a kiṃnarī looking upon her son bound in chains.

sanskrit: tathā tu vilapantīṃ tāṃ kausalyāṃ rāmamātaram uvāca lakṣmaṇo dīnas tat kālasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ
english: To Kausalyā, Rāma's mother, lamenting thus, Lakṣmaṇa, stricken with sorrow, spoke words befitting that moment.

sanskrit: na rocate mamāpy etad ārye yad rāghavo vanam tyaktvā rājyaśriyaṃ gacchet striyā vākyavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: "It does not please me either, O noble lady, that Rāghava should go to the forest, abandoning royal splendor, having been subjected to the words of a woman."

sanskrit: viparītaś ca vṛddhaś ca viṣayaiś ca pradharṣitaḥ nṛpaḥ kim iva na brūyāc codyamānaḥ samanmathaḥ
english: "A king who has changed in character, who is old, and who has been overpowered by the senses — what might such a one not say when provoked while in the grip of passion?"

sanskrit: nāsyāparādhaṃ paśyāmi nāpi doṣaṃ tathā vidham yena nirvāsyate rāṣṭrād vanavāsāya rāghavaḥ
english: "I see no offense in him, nor any fault of that kind, on account of which Rāghava should be banished from the kingdom to dwell in the forest."

sanskrit: na taṃ paśyāmy ahaṃ loke parokṣam api yo naraḥ amitro 'pi nirasto 'pi yo 'sya doṣam udāharet
english: "I see no one in the world — not even speaking behind his back — no man, enemy or estranged, who would name a fault in him."

sanskrit: devakalpam ṛjuṃ dāntaṃ ripūṇām api vatsalam avekṣamāṇaḥ ko dharmaṃ tyajet putram akāraṇāt
english: "Who, bearing in mind dharma, would abandon without cause a son who is godlike, upright, self-restrained, tender even toward his enemies?"

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vacanaṃ rājñaḥ punar bālyam upeyuṣaḥ putraḥ ko hṛdaye kuryād rājavṛttam anusmaran
english: "What son, keeping in mind the conduct proper to kings, would take to heart this word of a king who has reverted to childhood?"

sanskrit: yāvad eva na jānāti kaś cid artham imaṃ naraḥ tāvad eva mayā sārdham ātmasthaṃ kuru śāsanam
english: "As long as no person knows of this matter, until then, establish your authority while it rests in yourself — act jointly with me."

sanskrit: mayā pārśve sadhanuṣā tava guptasya rāghava kaḥ samartho 'dhikaṃ kartuṃ kṛtāntasyeva tiṣṭhataḥ
english: "With me standing at your side bearing my bow, protecting you, O Rāghava, who is capable of doing you harm — as if standing against Death himself?"

sanskrit: nirmanuṣyām imāṃ sarvām ayodhyāṃ manujarṣabha kariṣyāmi śarais tīkṣṇair yadi sthāsyati vipriye
english: "I shall empty this entire Ayodhyā of men with sharp arrows if she persists in this wrong, O bull among men."

sanskrit: bharatasyātha pakṣyo vā yo vāsya hitam icchati sarvān etān vadhiṣyāmi mṛdur hi paribhūyate
english: "Whoever sides with Bharata or wishes his good — all of them I shall slay; for the gentle are always overpowered."

sanskrit: tvayā caiva mayā caiva kṛtvā vairam anuttamam kasya śaktiḥ śriyaṃ dātuṃ bharatāyāriśāsana
english: "With both you and me as his unsurpassed enemies, who has the power to give sovereignty to Bharata, O chastiser of foes?"

sanskrit: anurakto 'smi bhāvena bhrātaraṃ devi tattvataḥ satyena dhanuṣā caiva datteneṣṭena te śape
english: "I am genuinely devoted with my whole being to my brother, O queen — I swear to you by truth, by my bow, and by the sacrificial offerings I have made."

sanskrit: dīptam agnim araṇyaṃ vā yadi rāmaḥ pravekṣyate praviṣṭaṃ tatra māṃ devi tvaṃ pūrvam avadhāraya
english: "If Rāma enters a blazing fire or the wilderness, know me, O queen, as having already entered there before him."

sanskrit: harāmi vīryād duḥkhaṃ te tamaḥ sūrya ivoditaḥ devī paśyatu me vīryaṃ rāghavaś caiva paśyatu
english: "I shall remove your sorrow by my valor, as the risen sun disperses darkness — let the queen behold my prowess, and let Rāghava behold it."

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ uvāca rāmaṃ kausalyā rudantī śokalālasā
english: Having heard these words of the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Kausalyā, weeping and distracted with grief, spoke to Rāma.

sanskrit: bhrātus te vadataḥ putra lakṣmaṇasya śrutaṃ tvayā yad atrānantaraṃ tat tvaṃ kuruṣva yadi rocate
english: "My son, you have heard what your brother Lakṣmaṇa has said — do accordingly whatever follows from that, if it pleases you."

sanskrit: na cādharmyaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sapatnyā mama bhāṣitam vihāya śokasaṃtaptāṃ gantum arhasi mām itaḥ
english: "And you ought not to depart from here, leaving me scorched with grief, after hearing the unrighteous words spoken by my co-wife."

sanskrit: dharmajña yadi dharmiṣṭho dharmaṃ caritum icchasi śuśrūṣa mām ihasthas tvaṃ cara dharmam anuttamam
english: "O knower of dharma, if you are righteous and wish to practice dharma, then serve me, remaining here — practice the highest dharma."

sanskrit: śuśrūṣur jananīṃ putra svagṛhe niyato vasan pareṇa tapasā yuktaḥ kāśyapas tridivaṃ gataḥ
english: "Serving his mother, my son, Kaśyapa, dwelling restrained in his own home, endowed with the highest austerity, attained the three heavens."

sanskrit: yathaiva rājā pūjyas te gauraveṇa tathā hy aham tvāṃ nāham anujānāmi na gantavyam ito vanam
english: "Just as the king is to be honored by you with reverence, so too am I — I do not give you permission; you must not go to the forest from here."

sanskrit: tvadviyogān na me kāryaṃ jīvitena sukhena vā tvayā saha mama śreyas tṛṇānām api bhakṣaṇam
english: "Without you, life holds no purpose for me, nor happiness — with you beside me, even eating grass is my greater good."

sanskrit: yadi tvaṃ yāsyasi vanaṃ tyaktvā māṃ śokalālasām ahaṃ prāyam ihāsiṣye na hi śakṣyāmi jīvitum
english: "If you go to the forest leaving me here consumed with grief, I shall sit here in a fast unto death — I shall not be able to live."

sanskrit: tatas tvaṃ prāpsyase putra nirayaṃ lokaviśrutam brahmahatyām ivādharmāt samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ
english: "Then you, my son, shall attain the hell renowned in the world, just as the lord of rivers, the ocean, receives the sin of brahminicide through unrighteousness."

sanskrit: vilapantīṃ tathā dīnāṃ kausalyāṃ jananīṃ tataḥ uvāca rāmo dharmātmā vacanaṃ dharmasaṃhitam
english: Then the righteous-souled Rāma spoke words suffused with dharma to his mother Kausalyā, lamenting thus in her misery.

sanskrit: nāsti śaktiḥ pitur vākyaṃ samatikramituṃ mama prasādaye tvāṃ śirasā gantum icchāmy ahaṃ vanam
english: "I have no power to transgress my father's word — I bow my head and beseech you: I wish to go to the forest."

sanskrit: ṛṣiṇā ca pitur vākyaṃ kurvatā vratacāriṇā gaur hatā jānatā dharmaṃ kaṇḍunāpi vipaścitā
english: "Even the learned sage Kaṇḍu, practitioner of vows, while carrying out his father's command — knowing dharma — slew a cow."

sanskrit: asmākaṃ ca kule pūrvaṃ sagarasyājñayā pituḥ khanadbhiḥ sāgarair bhūtim avāptaḥ sumahān vadhaḥ
english: "And in our own lineage of old, by the Sāgaras who dug at their father Sagara's command, a most great destruction was accomplished."

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa reṇukā jananī svayam kṛttā paraśunā araṇye pitur vacanakāriṇā
english: "By Rāma Jāmadagnya, carrying out his father's command, his own mother Reṇukā was herself slain with an axe in the forest."

sanskrit: na khalv etan mayaikena kriyate pitṛśāsanam pūrvair ayam abhipreto gato mārgo 'nugamyate
english: "This adherence to a father's command is not being done by me alone — this path, intended by the ancients, is being followed in their footsteps."

sanskrit: tad etat tu mayā kāryaṃ kriyate bhuvi nānyathā pitur hi vacanaṃ kurvan na kaś cin nāma hīyate
english: "This therefore must be done by me on earth, and no otherwise — for one who carries out his father's word never comes to diminishment."

sanskrit: tām evam uktvā jananīṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ punar abravīt tava lakṣmaṇa jānāmi mayi sneham anuttamam abhiprāyam avijñāya satyasya ca śamasya ca
english: Having thus addressed his mother, he spoke again to Lakṣmaṇa: "I know, Lakṣmaṇa, your unsurpassed love for me, though the purport of truth and of tranquility has not been understood."

sanskrit: dharmo hi paramo loke dharme satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam dharmasaṃśritam etac ca pitur vacanam uttamam
english: "For dharma is supreme in the world; truth is grounded in dharma; and this highest word of my father rests upon dharma."

sanskrit: saṃśrutya ca pitur vākyaṃ mātur vā brāhmaṇasya vā na kartavyaṃ vṛthā vīra dharmam āśritya tiṣṭhatā
english: "Having pledged to a father's word, or a mother's, or a Brāhmaṇa's, one standing firm in dharma must not make it vain, O hero."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ na śakṣyāmi pitur niyogam ativartitum pitur hi vacanād vīra kaikeyyāhaṃ pracoditaḥ
english: "I am not able to transgress my father's command — for it is by my father's word, O hero, that Kaikeyī has sent me forth."

sanskrit: tad enāṃ visṛjānāryāṃ kṣatradharmāśritāṃ matim dharmam āśraya mā taikṣṇyaṃ madbuddhir anugamyatām
english: "Therefore abandon this ignoble resolve rooted in the dharma of warriors, take refuge in dharma, set aside harshness — let my counsel be followed."

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā sauhārdād bhrātaraṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ uvāca bhūyaḥ kausalyāṃ prāñjaliḥ śirasānataḥ
english: Having thus spoken out of affection to his brother, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa spoke again to Kausalyā, with joined palms and bowed head.

sanskrit: anumanyasva māṃ devi gamiṣyantam ito vanam śāpitāsi mama prāṇaiḥ kuru svastyayanāni me tīrṇapratijñaś ca vanāt punar eṣyāmy ahaṃ purīm
english: "Grant me permission, O queen, as I go to the forest from here — I swear to you by my life: perform the auspicious rites for me; having fulfilled my vow, I shall return again from the forest to the city."

sanskrit: yaśo hy ahaṃ kevalarājyakāraṇān na pṛṣṭhataḥ kartum alaṃ mahodayam adīrghakāle na tu devi jīvite vṛṇe 'varām adya mahīm adharmataḥ
english: "For I am not able to bring about great prosperity behind the back of renown merely for the sake of the kingdom in a short while — nor, O queen, do I today choose a lesser earth through unrighteousness over life."

sanskrit: prasādayan naravṛṣabhaḥ sa mātaraṃ parākramāj jigamiṣur eva daṇḍakān athānujaṃ bhṛśam anuśāsya darśanaṃ cakāra tāṃ hṛdi jananīṃ pradakṣiṇam
english: That bull among men, still intent on going to the Daṇḍaka forest by his own valor, propitiating his mother, and then firmly instructing his younger brother, made a final appearance, circumambulated his mother in his heart, and took his leave.
